findings.message: Outcome guarantee or absolute claim; not allowed in dental advertising.

findings.quote: we promise a visibly brighter smile after a single visit
findings.why: This guarantees a specific result, which ADA advertising rules prohibit. It also contradicts the post's own statement that results vary by person and stain type.
findings.fix: Delete the promise and say that most patients see some lightening but results vary, as the post already says.

findings.quote: The ADA's [MouthHealthy page on teeth whitening](https://www.mouthhealthy.org/all-topics-a-z/tooth-whitening-safety) covers the basics.
findings.why: I cannot confirm that this exact URL exists, though the domain and topic are plausible for the ADA's consumer site.
findings.fix: Open the link before publishing and replace it with the correct MouthHealthy or ADA URL if it does not resolve.

findings.quote: Whitening is one of the most requested cosmetic treatments, and one of the most misunderstood.
findings.why: This is a harmless general statement, but it has no source and cannot be checked.
findings.fix: Soften it to something like 'Whitening is a popular cosmetic treatment' or add a source.

findings.quote: At-home kits are cheaper and slower, and results depend on how consistently you use them.
findings.why: This is a broad generalization with no source, though it is plausible and low risk.
findings.fix: Hedge it with 'often' or 'typically', or cite an ADA source.
